standard_prerequisites.name: A pure ideal I satisfies I^2 = I
The module of differentials of B over A is I/I^2 where I is the kernel of the multiplication map B tensor_A B -> B
standard_prerequisites.use: Expresses Omega_{B/A} as the vanishing quotient.

standard_prerequisites.name: A ring map B over A is formally unramified if and only if Omega_{B/A} = 0
standard_prerequisites.use: Converts the vanishing into formal unramifiedness.

core_obligations: Let I be the kernel of the multiplication map B tensor_A B -> B; by hypothesis this map is flat and surjective, so I is a pure ideal, and pure ideals are idempotent, I^2 = I (proof lines 30424-30427). The module of differentials is Omega_{B/A} = I/I^2 by the differentials-diagonal lemma, so it vanishes (proof lines 30428-30429). By the characterization of formally unramified maps, the vanishing of Omega_{B/A} means B is formally unramified over A (proof lines 30430-30432).
proof_roadmap: Identify I as pure, hence idempotent (proof lines 30424-30427).
Compute Omega_{B/A} = I/I^2 = 0 and conclude formal unramifiedness (proof lines 30428-30432).
